skill.name: adaptyv
skill.description: Use Adaptyv to plan protein validation experiments, submit sequences through the API, track experiment status, retrieve results, and apply protein optimization workflows before wet-lab testing.
skill.summary: Guide Adaptyv protein validation workflows from sequence design to lab result retrieval.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation for Adaptyv protein validation workflows and contains real outbound API usage. Most high and critical static findings are false positives caused by placeholders, markdown code fences, `.env` examples, or biological sequence terminology. No prompt injection text or hidden malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: External API and prediction service calls handle protein sequences and metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly disclose all external services and require user approval before submitting confidential sequences.

remediation.issue: API token examples rely on local environment variables and `.env` files.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing warnings and add a reminder to exclude `.env` files from shared logs and support bundles.

remediation.issue: The Adaptyv endpoint is an opaque AWS Lambda URL rather than a branded API domain.
remediation.suggestion: Document the official endpoint provenance or replace it with a stable branded domain when available.

content.value_statement: Protein design teams need a clear path from generated sequences to lab validation. This skill guides Adaptyv API setup, experiment submission, status tracking, result retrieval, and optimization workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains Adaptyv API authentication, base endpoints, and request structure.
Provides workflows for single, batch, and webhook-backed experiment submissions.
Guides experiment status checks, result retrieval, and local result organization.
Summarizes binding, expression, thermostability, and enzyme activity assay workflows.
Describes sequence optimization with NetSolP, SoluProt, SolubleMPNN, and ESM.
Shows FASTA formatting and validation patterns for protein sequence submissions.
limitations: Requires user-provided Adaptyv API access and valid organization credits.
Uses external Adaptyv and prediction services, so users must approve data sharing.
Describes an alpha or beta API that may change without full backward compatibility.
Does not perform wet-lab work itself or guarantee assay success.

use_cases.title: Submit Design Libraries
use_cases.description: Prepare FASTA libraries and submit expression or binding assays through the Adaptyv API.

use_cases.title: Track Experiment Progress
use_cases.description: Check status, configure webhooks, and plan around expected result delivery windows.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Variants
use_cases.description: Filter protein candidates with solubility and naturalness scores before ordering lab validation.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up Adaptyv API access for protein testing. Explain the credentials, environment variables, and first connection check.

prompt_templates.title: Submit A Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: I have one protein sequence for expression testing. Guide me through FASTA formatting, request fields, and submission steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Batch Assay
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a batch validation plan for 50 antibody variants with metadata, target selection, webhook tracking, and result review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Then Validate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an optimization workflow that ranks protein variants with solubility and ESM checks before submitting the top candidates to Adaptyv.

output_examples.input: I need to test whether three variants express well.
output_examples.output: A submission checklist with FASTA preparation, expression assay selection, metadata fields, authentication reminders, and status tracking steps.

output_examples.input: My binding assay finished and I need to interpret results.
output_examples.output: A review outline covering affinity values, kinetic rates, quality metrics, confidence flags, and next iteration decisions.

output_examples.input: I want to improve a low-solubility sequence before testing.
output_examples.output: A staged optimization plan using solubility screening, sequence redesign, naturalness scoring, and final experimental validation.

best_practices: Confirm API access, credits, and data-sharing approval before submitting sequences.
Validate FASTA formatting and sequence quality locally before each experiment.
Use webhooks or controlled polling for long-running experiments.
anti_patterns: Do not commit API keys or `.env` files to version control.
Do not submit confidential protein sequences without organizational approval.
Do not treat computational scores as replacements for experimental validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan Adaptyv protein validation workflows, submit experiments, track status, retrieve results, and optimize sequences.

faq.question: Do I need an Adaptyv API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require a user-provided API token from Adaptyv.

faq.question: Can it run assays directly?
faq.answer: No. It guides API workflows for a cloud laboratory service that performs the experimental work.

faq.question: Does it send data to external services?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflows submit protein sequences and metadata to Adaptyv or prediction services.

faq.question: What experiment types are covered?
faq.answer: It covers binding assays, expression testing, thermostability measurements, and enzyme activity assays.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
